checks.description: Employment excludes this unemployment benefit

results.question: What happens if the household cannot pay this week's rent?
results.scope: Actual rental phase; one occupied unit at $20/week, $40 weekly wage, balances as shown at rent collection, no cheaper alternative.

checks.description: Insufficient liquid funds end the tenancy
Cash or funded deposit withdrawal can cover rent
Rent received equals the household's cash and deposit loss

findings: The rental rule still has immediate eviction when rent cannot be paid. Wages now arrive before this phase in a complete default week; a cheaper available home could also change its outcome.

results.question: What if there is only enough money for part of a loan payment?
results.scope: Actual registered-loan collection; $10 due and remaining cash as shown. Wages now arrive before this phase in a complete default week.

checks.description: Collection cannot take more cash than the borrower has
Borrower payments reach the bank
Unpaid contractual balances remain outstanding

findings: In the default collector, a partial positive payment improves credit and does not count as a missed payment. That is a rule to review.

results.question: Does a business change its plan when customers disappear?

results.question: What happens when a business cannot afford payroll?
results.scope: Actual production-cost and household-income phases; two retained workers at $40 each, no sales or taxes in this fixture.

checks.description: The business debit equals workers' receipts

findings: The default payroll path pays the full wage bill and permits negative business cash. Zero cash does not by itself stop wages in this phase.
